title: Tiny CRM
metaTitle: Tiny CRM — A CRM for Small Teams · Artifact Digital
description: Our own product: projects, contacts, deals, RFPs, tasks and notes in one workspace, built around a single question — what needs my attention today?

card.blurb: A CRM for people running the whole business, not a sales department — with the day's priorities on the first screen.
card.imageAlt: Five phone screens from Tiny CRM: Tiny AI, the daily brief, opportunities, quick add and projects.

lede: Tiny CRM pulls projects, contacts, companies, deals, RFPs, tasks and notes into one workspace, and opens on the only question that matters on a Monday: what needs my attention today? We designed and built it as our own product.
pillarsHeading: Small teams get the leftovers of enterprise software.

pillars.title: Everything lived somewhere else
pillars.body: Projects in one tool, contacts in another, tasks in a third, RFPs in a spreadsheet, and the notes that explain any of it wherever someone happened to type them.

pillars.title: Enterprise CRM became the default
pillars.body: The big platforms are built for sales organizations with an administrator to run them. A team of two or five inherits all of that structure and none of the staff to maintain it.

pillars.title: The dashboard answered the wrong question
pillars.body: Most dashboards report how many. The person running the business needs to know which thing is slipping, who has gone quiet, and what to do before lunch.

storyHeadingLines.text: The CRM shouldn't be the work.
It should tell you where the work is.

storyParagraphs: Every screen answers one of four questions: what is happening, who is involved, what needs my attention, what should I do next. Where a bigger product offers a settings page, Tiny picks a default.

So it opens on a Daily Brief rather than a chart, and Tiny AI reads your own data from behind a keyboard shortcut instead of a chat bubble on every screen. Underneath: Postgres with row-level security, per-record grants, and a security suite among seventy-five test files.
storyImageAlt: Tiny CRM on a laptop and a phone: the marketing page above the product, showing the daily brief and pipeline.
storyCaption: The pitch and the product share a promise: your whole business, organized. Figures shown are demo data.

highlights.title: One place to run the work
highlights.body: Projects, contacts, companies, deals, RFPs, tasks, notes, calendar and files reference each other instead of living in separate tools.

highlights.title: AI that reads your own data
highlights.body: The Daily Brief and Tiny AI surface what needs attention, behind ⌘K and a keyboard shortcut rather than a chatbot on every screen.

highlights.title: Security treated as a feature
highlights.body: Row-level security, workspace isolation and per-record grants, with a security test suite that runs alongside the rest.

highlights.title: Built to keep evolving
highlights.body: Forty-one screens and ten API routes on one data model, so new workflows get added without rebuilding the product.
